title: Travel Booking Platform • Decision-Driven UX
subtitle: Helping users move from vague intent to confident booking
coverAlt: My Perfect Greek Vacation concept cover

facts.label: scope
value: End-to-end UX architecture of a travel booking platform focused on improving decision-making before booking
Behavior modeling, UX system design, interaction logic, decision flow architecture

facts.label: audience
value: Users planning vacations without a clear destination

facts.label: focus
value: Shift the experience from search & browse to guided decision-making before booking

value.text:
My Perfect Greek Vacation is a concept for a travel booking platform designed for users who want to go on a vacation but cannot yet define what exactly they are looking for.

Instead of optimizing for search and inventory exposure, the product focuses on structuring user intent before presenting options.

The goal was to transform vague travel desire into a clear, decision-ready state — and only then move to booking.
Users cannot confidently choose a travel option. Symptoms include opening multiple tabs, inconsistent comparison, lack of criteria, and postponed decisions.
Large inventory space, no initial user clarity, high emotional + financial stakes, and limited decision time.

Users approach travel booking as a risk-heavy decision under uncertainty. Behavior patterns include over-scrolling, fragmented comparison, reliance on external validation, and inability to commit. They are not solving a search problem — they are solving a decision problem.
The core problem in travel booking is not lack of options. It is lack of decision clarity.

Introduce a decision-first architecture: capture user preferences early, convert them into structured input, map preferences to relevant options, provide reasoning for each option, enable confident decision before booking.
Replace search with preference capture, limit visible options, add reasoning to each option, separate decision from booking, introduce iterative loop.

items: Breadth vs Clarity — Limit options to improve decision-making
Speed vs Confidence — Add upfront steps to increase decision quality
Control vs Guidance — Reduce free exploration in favor of structured flow
Funnel vs Loop — Support iterative behavior instead of forcing linear flow

value.text: A travel booking platform that captures user intent early, reduces option space, provides curated recommendations, explains each option, and enables confident booking.

North Star Metric: Decision Confidence Rate — percentage of users who proceed to booking without returning to exploration. Supporting metrics include Time to Decision, Option Exploration Depth, Preference Refinement Rate, Decision Drop-off Rate, and Booking Conversion Rate.
